title: Unramified group schemes detected by dual numbers at the identity
statement: Let $K$ be a field and $G$ a group scheme of finite type over $K$, with identity $e:\operatorname{Spec}K\to G$ [def-weil-field, def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $D=\operatorname{Spec}(K[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$ [def-sc-dual-numbers], let $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\hookrightarrow D$ set $\epsilon=0$, and let $p:D\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ be the structure map. Then $G\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] if and only if every $K$-morphism $v:D\to G$ satisfying $v\circ i=e$ equals $e\circ p$. No smoothness, reducedness, or assumption on the characteristic of $K$ is imposed.

proof.text: Write $f:G\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, $\Omega=\Omega^1_{G/K}$ and $M=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}K,e^*\Omega)$. The unit identity gives $f\circ e=\mathrm{id}$, so $e$ is a $K$-rational point. Explicitly the field maps $K\to\kappa(e)\to K$ have composite identity; the second is injective and its image contains $K$, so they are inverse isomorphisms. A module sheaf on the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is determined by its $K$-vector space of sections; hence $e^*\Omega=0$ if and only if $M=0$.

source.place: Tag 0E6G, label lemma-in-DM-locus-vector-fields, first proof paragraph: kappa(e) = k.

proof.text: The set of $K$-morphisms $v:D\to G$ with $v\circ i=e$ is exactly $T_{G/K,e}$. Its zero is $e\circ p$: multiplying any tangent vector by the scalar $0$ precomposes it with the dual-number map $\epsilon\mapsto0$, namely $i\circ p$. Thus the condition in the statement is precisely $T_{G/K,e}=0$. Apply the rational tangent/differential-fibre duality at the rational point $e$ to obtain $T_{G/K,e}\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(M,K)$. Consequently the stated condition is equivalent to $\operatorname{Hom}_K(M,K)=0$.

source.place: Tags 0B2C (definition-tangent-space) and 0B2D (lemma-tangent-space-cotangent-space), at the rational identity.

proof.text: The vanishing $\operatorname{Hom}_K(M,K)=0$ is equivalent to $M=0$. For the nontrivial implication, apply the dual-map criterion to the unique linear map $u:0\to M$. If the dual of $M$ is zero, then $u^*:M^*\to0^*$ is injective. The cited criterion makes $u$ surjective, and thus every element of $M$ is zero. Conversely a functional on the zero vector space is zero. No finite-dimensionality is used.

source.place: Tag 0E6G, first proof paragraph, the linear-algebra implication from zero tangent space to zero cotangent fibre.

proof.text: Apply the group-scheme differential isomorphism to obtain $\Omega\cong f^*e^*\Omega$. If $M=0$, step 1 gives $e^*\Omega=0$ and the right side is zero: in the tensor formula for module pullback every pure tensor has zero second factor. Hence $\Omega=0$. Conversely $\Omega=0$ implies $e^*\Omega=0$ by that same pullback formula, so $M=0$. This proves $M=0\Longleftrightarrow\Omega=0$ on all of $G$, without assuming that $G$ is affine, smooth or reduced.

source.place: Tag 047I, label lemma-group-scheme-module-differentials, pulled-back identity differential sheaf.

proof.text: Finally $f$ is locally of finite type, since it is of finite type. Choose its affine cover $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a finitely generated $K$-algebra. The affine differential-sections equivalence identifies $\Gamma(U,\Omega)$ with $\Omega_{A/K}$. If $\Omega=0$, each $\Omega_{A/K}$ is zero, so this cover satisfies the affine unramified criterion stated in the unramified definition. Conversely, if $f$ is unramified, that definition supplies an affine cover with $\Omega_{A/K}=0$; the differential-sheaf definition identifies $\Omega|_U$ with the sheaf associated to this zero module, so $\Omega|_U=0$. These opens cover $G$, giving $\Omega=0$. Thus $f$ is unramified if and only if $\Omega=0$. Together with steps 2--4 this is exactly the desired equivalence.
